item.title: Saraki cautions Kwara Gov over treatment of traditional rulers
item.description: Former Senate President, Dr Abubakar Bukola Saraki, has urged Kwara State Governor Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq to respect traditional rulers and allow them receive political leaders across party lines. Saraki made the call following allegations that the governor had summoned some traditional rulers to Ilorin and threatened to suspend those who received leaders of the opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) during courtesy visits to their palaces. In a statement personally signed by him, Saraki said the alleged actions followed his stakeholder engagements in Kwara North Senatorial District, which began last week. He explained that visits to traditional rulers were part of established customs and protocols, adding that the royal fathers should be allowed to receive political leaders regardless of their party affiliations. Saraki said traditional rulers were fathers of all and should not be subjected to pressure over their interactions with politicians. He also urged the leadership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to caution Abdulrazaq, saying political differences should not prevent opposition parties from engaging communities and traditional institutions. The former Senate President recalled that during the 16 years the PDP governed Kwara State, traditional rulers were not prevented from receiving opposition leaders. He said democracy required tolerance of opposing views and urged the governor to respect the state’s traditional institutions. Saraki, however, insisted that the alleged actions would not discourage the PDP from continuing its engagements across the state. He said the party would sustain its outreach to communities in the three senatorial districts, adding that the response to its engagements had been encouraging. item.title: Senate Appropriations Committee session turns violent as aide, security operatives clash
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — A legislative aide to Senator Allwell Onyesoh (Rivers East) was allegedly assaulted by security operatives attached to the Senate Committee on Appropriations, chaired by Senator Olamilekan Adeola (APC, Ogun West), during a confrontation at the National Assembly complex, Abuja. The aide, Barrister Kingsley Wali, reportedly sustained head injuries during the incident and was rushed to the National Assembly Clinic for medical attention. Wali alleged that he and another aide to Senator Onyesoh, identified as Dr Kingsley, were attacked by security personnel after accompanying their principal to an Appropriations Committee meeting. Recounting the incident, Wali said the confrontation occurred after Senator Onyesoh had entered the committee room and he attempted to follow him. He said security personnel at the entrance were trying to close the door and stopped him from entering. According to him, when the operatives attempted to push his colleague away, he explained that their principal had already entered the room and that they were not attempting to force their way inside. He alleged that the situation escalated when the security personnel grabbed Dr Kingsley by the neck and began assaulting him. “I kept telling them to leave him alone because he is our senator’s personal assistant and my colleague. I even held one of the security personnel’s hands and pleaded with him to stop beating him,” Wali said. He further alleged that the operatives turned on him because he intervened on behalf of his colleague. Wali claimed that one of the security personnel grabbed him and pushed him down a staircase, while three others allegedly cornered him and repeatedly hit his head with the butt of a gun. He said the assault continued until he slumped, after which the operatives left him. According to him, Dr Kingsley subsequently took photographs of his condition and sent them to Senator Onyesoh through WhatsApp while the senator was attending the committee meeting. Wali said the senator came out after receiving the photographs and found him lying in a pool of blood. He added that the senator subsequently took him into the committee room, where members expressed shock at his condition and directed that he be taken to the hospital for treatment. Speaking about his condition, Wali said he was still weak following the alleged assault and the fall. “I’m weak. I’m completely weak because they pushed me down and I slumped. But God will take care of everything. I thank God for everything,” he said. However, Senator Adeola’s Special Adviser on Media, Kayode Odunaro, offered a different account of the incident. In a statement titled, “Security Breach at Senate Committee on Appropriations Room,” Odunaro said the confrontation followed a misunderstanding between aides of some senators attempting to gain access to a committee room during a closed-door session and security personnel stationed at the entrance. item.title: ‘Name National Theatre after Pete Edochie, not Wole Soyinka’ – Brymo to Tinubu
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian singer, Brymo, has urged President Bola Tinubu to name the National Theatre after late veteran actor Pete Edochie instead of Nobel laureate Wole Soyinka, following the death of the Nollywood icon. Brymo made the appeal in a video shared on his official Instagram page on Wednesday, where he paid tribute to Edochie and called on the President to reconsider the naming of the national cultural landmark. “Dear President Tinubu, name the National Theatre after Pete Edochie, not Wole Soyinka, please,” the singer said. He also celebrated the late actor, saying, “Cheers to one of the greatest men, Pete Edochie. May you live forever in our hearts, and on our screens.” Edochie died at the age of 79, with his death announced on Wednesday, November 25, 2026. His passing has prompted tributes from political leaders, colleagues and members of the entertainment industry. President Tinubu, in a tribute, described the late actor as one of Africa’s most recognisable thespians and a pioneer of Nigeria’s film industry. He also recalled Edochie’s portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart in the 1980s. The President praised his performances in productions including Igodo , Rituals and Lionheart , saying his work helped project Nigeria’s cultural heritage and storytelling traditions to audiences around the world. Brymo’s appeal comes against the backdrop of the Federal Government’s decision to rename the National Theatre in Iganmu, Lagos, after Soyinka in 2024, as part of the celebration of the literary icon’s 90th birthday. Tinubu announced that the facility would be known as the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts. The renovated complex was formally commissioned under the new name on October 1, 2025, during Nigeria’s 65th Independence anniversary celebrations. The President had described the renaming as an honour for Soyinka, whose contributions to literature, theatre and human rights advocacy have earned him international recognition, including the 1986 Nobel Prize in Literature. item.title: FG orders probe as three inmates die after Ilorin jailbreak
item.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin The Federal Government has ordered an investigation into the deaths of three condemned inmates at the Oke-Kura Custodial Centre in Ilorin, Kwara State, following a jailbreak attempt last week. The Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, who ordered the investigation, described the deaths as unfortunate and vowed that anyone found culpable would face the full weight of the law. The minister, who visited the facility on Wednesday to assess the situation, also expressed concern that more than 70 condemned inmates at the centre had spent over 10 years on death row, attributing the prolonged stay to delays by state authorities in exercising their powers to grant clemency or commute death sentences. The minister was represented during the visit by the Comptroller-General of the Nigerian Correctional Service, Mr Sylvester Nwakuche, who briefed journalists after inspecting the facility. Nwakuche said he returned to Ilorin on the minister’s directive to investigate reports surrounding the incident and assess the condition of the facility. According to him, seven condemned inmates attempted to breach the security of the custodial centre during the jailbreak, but only two succeeded in escaping. He said the remaining five were apprehended and returned to custody, but three subsequently died. “Two succeeded in making their way out of the facility, while the remaining five could not. They were taken back, but unfortunately, we were informed that three out of the five who could not escape lost their lives. “That is an unfortunate incident, and the minister wanted us to come immediately to assess the situation,” he said. The Comptroller-General said a team had been constituted to investigate the deaths, adding that the inquiry would involve clinical, medical and intelligence processes. He assured that the two escaped inmates would be rearrested, regardless of how long it took. Nwakuche also disclosed that more than 70 condemned inmates were being held at the Oke-Kura facility, with some having spent over a decade on death row. He described the situation as a major challenge, noting that the colonial-era facility was accommodating nearly 685 inmates and was severely overcrowded. He said the problem extended beyond Ilorin, disclosing that more than 4,000 inmates were on death row across correctional facilities nationwide. The Comptroller-General appealed to state governors to exercise their constitutional powers by considering the commutation of death sentences to life imprisonment, where appropriate. According to him, such action would enable the Correctional Service to transfer affected inmates to less congested facilities, where they could undergo rehabilitation and vocational training. “We have been appealing to the necessary authorities, the governors, to do what the law permits them to do. item.title: FG Launches ₦1.45trn Lagos Ports Modernisation, Targets 48-Hour Cargo Clearance
item.description: The Federal Government has flagged off the modernisation and upgrade of the Lagos Port Complex, Apapa, and Tin Can Island Port. The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, supported by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr Taiwo Oyedele, and other senior government officials, unveiled the project on Wednesday, describing it as a strategic investment that will reposition Nigeria as a leading maritime hub in Africa and strengthen the country’s competitiveness in global trade. Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony at the Tin-Can Island Port, Oyetola said the project, which would cost £746 million (approximately ₦1.45 trillion), would address decades of infrastructure deficits, reduce logistics costs, attract international shipping lines, stimulate industrial growth and create at least 20,000 direct and indirect jobs. The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, said the project, which would cost £746 million (approximately ₦1.45 trillion), would address decades of infrastructure deficits (X/@GboyegaOyetola) He said the modernisation programme was a significant step towards realising President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, which prioritises infrastructure development as a catalyst for economic growth, investment and job creation. According to the minister, the two ports, which have served as major gateways for Nigeria’s international commerce for decades, have become increasingly inadequate to meet the demands of a rapidly expanding economy and changing global shipping requirements. He noted that Apapa Port, established in 1913, was more than a century old, while Tin Can Island Port was commissioned in 1977 when Nigeria’s population stood at approximately 67.2 million, annual trade was about $17 billion, and cargo throughput was 8.11 million metric tonnes. Today, he said, Nigeria’s population has grown to approximately 240 million, merchandise trade exceeds $100 billion annually, while cargo throughput has increased to 129.3 million metric tonnes, nearly 16 times its 1977 level. Oyetola stressed that the mismatch between growing economic activities and ageing port infrastructure had made comprehensive modernisation both urgent and unavoidable. “The cost of inaction is far greater than the cost of modernisation,” he was quoted as saying in a statement by the special adviser to the minister, Bolaji Akinola, as saying, adding that Nigeria will not surrender its competitive advantage. “Our ambition is to attract more direct calls by international shipping lines, retain Nigerian-bound cargo, expand transshipment opportunities and establish our ports as preferred gateways to trade across the African Continental Free Trade Area. We cannot achieve this ambition with infrastructure that falls behind the demands of modern shipping,” the minister said. item.title: Delta Killings: Reps urge Tinubu to consider emergency measures
item.description: By Gift CmapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has urged President Bola Tinubu to consider invoking constitutional emergency measures in Delta State if escalating political violence degenerates into a breakdown of public order and public safety. The lawmakers also called for a comprehensive investigation into successive attacks on political gatherings across the state, demanding the arrest and prosecution of perpetrators, sponsors and financiers of the violence. The resolutions followed the adoption of a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by the member representing Okpe/Sapele/Uvwie Federal Constituency, Delta State, Benedict Etanabene, during Wednesday’s plenary. The intervention comes against the backdrop of the November 23 attack on the campaign activities of former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, at Uduere community in Ughelli North Local Government Area, which claimed six lives and left several others injured. Presenting the motion, Etanabene expressed concern over the growing pattern of violence targeting political activities, warning that the attacks were creating an atmosphere of fear among political parties, candidates, supporters and residents. He recalled that violence broke out on November 7 during a political procession along Nnebisi Road, Asaba, resulting in one death and injuries to five persons, according to police figures. He also cited the November 11 attack on a political party’s campaign team at Okpai, Ward 4, Ndokwa East Local Government Area, which reportedly left five members injured. The lawmaker further recalled an incident in September during a political mobilisation exercise in Effurun, Uvwie Local Government Area, where a participant sustained machete injuries and later died in hospital. Etanabene said the latest attack at Uduere, where at least six people were reportedly killed by suspected political thugs, underscored the need for decisive intervention by the Federal Government and security agencies. He warned that the increasing frequency of attacks could trigger a wider breakdown of law and order, undermine peaceful coexistence and threaten the credibility of the 2027 general elections. The lawmaker also expressed concern that the recurrence of violence suggested that existing security arrangements were inadequate to deter perpetrators and protect political actors and innocent citizens. Consequently, the House urged Tinubu, in his capacity as Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, to direct relevant security agencies to take immediate steps to prevent further violence and loss of lives in the state. It also urged the Inspector-General of Police to deploy adequate personnel, including tactical and intelligence units, to identified security flashpoints across Delta State. item.title: Tinubu’s govt has made everyone poor — Obi
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of worsening poverty in the country, saying Nigerians should not continue to endure the hardship. Obi said his proposed government with former Kano State Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso would prioritise job creation, production, poverty reduction and the responsible management of public resources. He spoke on Wednesday at the NDC town hall meeting in Edo State, where he urged Nigerians to support the party in the 2027 general election. “Tinubu has put everybody into poverty; that poverty must not continue,” Obi said. The former Anambra State governor said his ambition was to move Nigeria away from a consumption-driven economy towards one focused on production, arguing that such a shift would create jobs and improve living conditions. “We want to build a new Nigeria that is possible. We want to remove Nigeria from consumption to production so all of you can have jobs. We want to pull Nigerians out of poverty, we want to build a country that cares for everybody,” he said. Obi also promised to tackle corruption and ensure that public resources were deployed for the benefit of citizens. “We want to build a country, where people will no longer steal public money. Public money must be used for public good. That’s what we want to do,” he said. Calling on supporters to remain vigilant during the 2027 elections, the NDC candidate urged voters to stay at their polling units after casting their ballots until the votes were counted. He said the party would not want its votes compromised through electoral malpractice. “We want you to go out in 2027, you’re our polling agents. When you vote, don’t go home. Stay there until your vote is counted. We don’t want them to rig us out. We must get it right this time because we want to build a better society,” Obi said. He urged Nigerians to vote for him and Kwankwaso, saying their proposed administration would be led by people committed to serving the country. “Vote Kwankwaso and I to start that new Nigeria. We want to make sure that we have a government of people, who have compassion, who have commitment, who have the energy to do the job,” he added. Obi further pledged to build a society where opportunities would not depend on personal connections or family background. “We want to build a society where a child of nobody can be somebody without knowing anybody,” he said. item.title: Bandits abduct six in midnight raid on Kaduna community
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Suspected bandits have abducted six residents during a midnight attack on Mama G area, near MPH, Millennium City, in Chikun Local Government Area of Kaduna State. The attackers reportedly stormed two houses around 11:30pm on Tuesday, shooting sporadically and initially abducting nine persons. However, three of the victims, including an elderly woman, a mother and her toddler, were later released, leaving six others in the custody of the abductors. The incident has heightened fears among residents of Millennium City, who say repeated attacks have made life increasingly difficult, forcing some homeowners and tenants to abandon their houses over fears of kidnapping. One of the residents, whose wife was among those abducted, was seen weeping as he appealed for help to secure her release. He expressed concern about her health, saying she had difficulty walking before the incident. “I don’t know her condition as we speak because she is having problems walking, and now they have taken her away. I’m appealing to whoever can help me rescue her from them,” he said. Another resident, Hassan Salihu, said residents heard gunshots around 11:30pm on Tuesday and immediately contacted one another to establish where the shooting was taking place. “When we heard gunshots, we started communicating with other residents to know the exact location. We later discovered it was here in our community. “We alerted the soldiers, and they came through Keke A and remained here until 4am, but we didn’t see the abductors leaving the area,” he said. Salihu appealed to the Kaduna State Government and security authorities to establish a military outpost in the community, particularly along routes allegedly used by the attackers. Similarly, Adamu Muhammad Maina said the attack threw residents into confusion, adding that nine people were initially taken from two neighbouring houses. “It was a terrible situation. Nine people were initially abducted from our neighbours’ houses. Four people were abducted from one house, including a woman and her toddler, but they were released,” he said. He explained that five other residents were taken from the second house, including an elderly woman who was subsequently released because of her inability to walk. “Now we have six people with the bandits, and nobody knows their location,” he added. A female resident, who pleaded anonymity, said the persistent attacks had traumatised the community, forcing some landlords and tenants to abandon their homes. “We are traumatised because most house owners are now abandoning their houses. We find it difficult to sleep inside our homes, so we are pleading with the relevant agencies, including the state and Federal Governments, to come to our aid,” she said. Residents also disclosed that suspected bandits had attempted to invade the community on Monday night but were repelled by security operatives before returning on Tuesday night. item.title: Southern Nigeria deserves eight years in presidency like North — Shehu Sani
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo Former Kaduna Central Senator, Shehu Sani, has said Southern Nigeria deserves to retain the Presidency for eight years, just as the North did under the All Progressives Congress (APC), in the interest of fairness, equity and justice. Sani said individual political ambitions should not be allowed to undermine the historical relationship, solidarity and common interests shared by the North and South. He spoke on Wednesday while delivering the second-term inauguration lecture of Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, in Osogbo. The former lawmaker said the principle of power rotation should be respected to ensure fairness between the two regions. “Like every other part of the country, the South deserves respect for the principle of political power rotation. Power has been held in the North for eight years. It should be allowed, in the spirit of fairness, equity and justice, to be in the South for eight years. “I am not saying this because I am in Osun State or because His Excellency is my friend or brother. Everyone who knows my history and has followed my public statements wherever I have spoken knows that this has always been my position. “The political ambitions of individuals should not be allowed to disrupt the good relationship, historical connections, commonality and solidarity that exist between the North and the South. We must not throw these values into the gutter because of the ambitions of individuals,” he said. Speaking on the theme, “Beyond the Ballot Box: Subnational Governance, Institutional Independence and the Future of Democracy in Nigeria,” Sani urged Adeleke to make his second term a period of institutional reforms, economic transformation and measurable development. He described the governor’s renewed mandate as a social contract that comes with greater expectations and responsibilities. He urged Adeleke to consolidate the achievements of his first term, address identified shortcomings and build strong institutions capable of surviving successive administrations. According to him, elections determine who occupies public offices, but strong institutions and effective governance determine whether political power translates into meaningful development. Sani also said President Bola Tinubu and Adeleke shared similar political DNA, although he did not elaborate on the comparison. In his remarks, Adeleke described Sani as a practical politician and intellectual with a deep understanding of Nigerian federalism. The governor acknowledged the challenges confronting the country’s federal structure, including excessive concentration of powers at the centre. He, however, expressed optimism that the Tinubu administration was taking steps towards restructuring the federation through constitutional amendments and the devolution of powers to states. “There is no doubt that Nigeria faces many challenges in its practice of federalism. item.title: Police arrest three suspects over political violence in Kebbi
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Police Command has arrested three suspects over alleged political violence during a political gathering in Zauro, Makera and surrounding communities in Birnin Kebbi Local Government Area. The arrests followed reports of violence and the alleged presence of individuals wielding dangerous weapons during political activities organised by members of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), ahead of the 2027 general elections. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman, disclosed this in a statement on Wednesday, saying preliminary investigations revealed that the gathering, reportedly presented as a distribution of relief materials, was organised by the wife of the ADC governorship candidate. According to him, the activities took place in Zauro, Makera, Gwadangwaji, Gawasu, Morida and Karyo without prior notification to the Police at least 48 hours before their commencement. Usman said the failure to notify the Police violated an agreement reached between the Command and political parties during a stakeholders’ engagement on September 7, 2026, as well as a subsequent meeting with the party’s caucus on November 2, 2026. He explained that during the meetings, the party had undertaken to notify the Commissioner of Police of all political activities at least 48 hours ahead to enable adequate security arrangements. The police spokesperson said video evidence obtained by the Command showed individuals in the convoy carrying sticks, machetes and swords, while some speakers allegedly made inciting statements capable of disrupting public peace. He added that some vehicles in the convoy were observed without registration numbers or with questionable number plates, while sirens were also used in violation of applicable traffic regulations. Usman said the Command condemned the conduct, warning that political activities must not degenerate into thuggery, violence or inflammatory statements. He said the Police would not tolerate any action capable of undermining public peace or setting a dangerous precedent ahead of the 2027 general elections. The Command urged the party’s leadership to honour its commitment to peaceful political engagement and cooperate with security agencies, including handing over individuals involved in unlawful conduct. Usman said the three suspects had been charged to court for prosecution, adding that any breach of agreed security protocols or applicable laws would be dealt with accordingly. The Command also called on relevant authorities to investigate reports of minors’ involvement in political activities and take appropriate measures to protect them from exploitation, violence and other harmful circumstances. item.title: Shettima ties Nigeria’s safety to economic stability
item.description: ‎–Says Tinubu confronts choices that could no longer be postponed to save the economy ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA– THE Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima has said that Nigeria cannot achieve genuine security without safeguarding the economic wellbeing and sustainable incomes of its citizens. ‎ ‎This, he said, explains why the administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has travelled across Nigeria to support small businesses through the MSME Clinics. ‎ ‎Speaking in Maiduguri, the Borno State capital, at the MSME Clinics and Artisans Beneficiary Town Hall, Senator Shettima said the administration acted on the conviction that Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) are the foundation of every economy. ‎ ‎”Whatever gains our reforms deliver in stabilising the economy, we cannot forget the hard truth that the strength of every nation rests on those who keep its people working. ‎ ‎”Your businesses, therefore, have never been a side attraction in our economic agenda. I am honoured to return home to Borno today to account for the progress we have made,” he stated. ‎ ‎The Vice President attributed the success of the MSME Clinics to the foresight of President Tinubu, who, according to him, understands that Nigeria cannot be secured “without securing the livelihoods of its people.” ‎ ‎”This presidential priority accords with the culture of public welfare that my dear brother, His Excellency, Governor Babagana Umara Zulum, has made the hallmark of his stewardship in Borno,” he added. ‎ ‎Acknowledging that the Tinubu administration inherited an economy on the brink of implosion, VP Shettima said the President “had to make choices that could no longer wait.” ‎ ‎He observed that while statistics and historical records could only explain so much, the language easily “understood by the man and woman on the street is the language of direct impact,” ‎ ‎Noting that this is why the administration made it a duty to improve their daily lives, he said, “Distinguished ladies and gentlemen, it is one thing to read about how a programme has helped a citizen. It is another to sit before that citizen and hear what changed. ‎ ‎”Meeting you today brings an intimacy to public service that no written report can offer. I am moved by your accounts just as much as I am strengthened by our obligation to do more.” ‎ ‎On the significance of the town hall, the VP said it was necessary because a beneficiary’s experience is the most eloquent feedback any government can receive. ‎ ‎He explained that beneficiaries are the ones who know what reached their workshop, what changed their working day, and what still stands in their way. ‎ ‎VP Shettima encouraged MSME Clinic beneficiaries to speak frankly about the obstacles they face, where they currently stand, and the steps required to address these challenges. ‎ ‎His words: “The task before our agencies is to turn those accounts into practical responses. item.title: ‘I’m done with Rivers, FCT; give me Imo, Kwara to deliver’ – Wike tells Tinubu
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has asked President Bola Tinubu and the Director General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, to assign him Imo and Kwara states, saying he has completed his political mobilisation work in Rivers State and the Federal Capital Territory. Wike made the request during a town hall meeting with residents and members of the Rainbow Coalition in Gokana Local Government Area of Rivers State. The minister said he had been assigned to coordinate Rivers and the FCT but was now seeking two additional states to work on ahead of the next election. “I was assigned to coordinate Rivers State and the FCT. Frankly speaking, I am done with these states, and we have no work to do again,” he said. Wike said he wanted the President and the campaign director general to give him more responsibilities, adding that he was willing to take charge of Imo State because of what he described as political challenges in the state. “As I am going now, I will plead with the Campaign DG and President Tinubu to add two more states for me to deliver. It’s a serious matter,” he said. He also referred to reports of divisions within the political structure in Kwara State, saying he would like to take responsibility for delivering the state for Tinubu. “From what I am told, they are having some problems in Imo State. So, I will like to go there and deliver Imo for Mr President,” Wike said. “Secondly, I have not confirmed, but what I read on social media is that there are some divisions in Kwara. So, I plead with the DG of the APC Presidential Council, Senator Yari, and Mr President to allow me to take over Imo and Kwara States, because I am done with Rivers and FCT,” he added. Wike’s remarks signal his willingness to take on a wider political mobilisation role in support of Tinubu, although he acknowledged that his information about the alleged divisions in Kwara was based on social media reports and had not been independently confirmed. item.title: [VIDEO] Insecurity: ‘We’ll Achieve Peace,’ Tinubu Assures Borno Residents, Urges Terrorists To Lay Down Arms
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has promised residents of Borno State that his administration is working to achieve lasting peace in the state. Tinubu, who stated this at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential rally in Maiduguri, Borno State, on Wednesday, also assured them that schoolchildren still in captivity will be rescued. The President, who said he was aware that residents were concerned about the security challenges, thanked them for their support, which he said contributed to the successes recorded so far. He also commended the Nigerian Armed Forces for their sacrifices for the nation. “We will achieve that peace. The terrorism will go. They have the opportunity now to lay down their arms, to lay down all arms and surrender all weapons, change from the character of terrorism and banditry,” he said. Tinubu, however, reiterated his call on registered voters to collect their permanent voter card and cast their votes for the APC in the 2027 general elections. Earlier, Vice President Kashim Shettima urged voters in the state to support the re-election of Tinubu in the January 16, 2027 election. Similarly, Governor Babagana Zulum said residents were witnessing the gradual return of peace to Borno State. He commended the APC-led Federal Government for the support it has rendered to the state. Zulum assured the President that Borno and North-East residents would vote en masse for him. He, however, appealed for the resumption of oil exploration in the region. item.title: NDLEA Dismantles Industrial-Scale Meth Lab In Enugu, Arrests Suspected Drug Baron, Five Mexicans
item.description: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said it has dismantled another industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratory in Enugu State. It also said that it arrested a 63-year-old drug baron it identified as one “Chuks Enoch Ezeike, popularly known as ‘Over Size’,” and five Mexican meth specialists whom he allegedly smuggled into the country with forged passports to produce the Class A drug on Nigerian soil. ﻿ The NDLEA disclosed that a total of 1,512 kilograms of methamphetamine, finished and in production, with an estimated value of US$226.8 million, equivalent to ₦303,913,000,000.00, was recovered from the clandestine factory, alongside 6.68 tons of 20 different types of precursor and essential chemicals and an array of industrial equipment for making the illicit substance. “Ezeike, a businessman who holds the traditional title of Ebekuo Dike na Nanka in his community in Anambra State, had built the industrial complex behind San Savanna Oil Company Limited, at Kilometre 1/2 Abakaliki Expressway, Emene, Enugu, complete with living quarters for the Mexicans so they could live and produce in the same place without being seen in town,” Chairman/Chief Executive Officer of the agency, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Marwa (retd.) said at a press conference in Abuja on Wednesday. Marwa described it as one of the most carefully planned, intelligence-led operations ever conducted by the agency, adding that the operation “began in faraway Mexico, ran through Colombia, France and the Republic of Benin, crossed into Lagos, and ended in an industrial complex in Enugu.” He explained that the agency’s Special Operations Unit (SOU) began working on critical intelligence in April 2026, which identified Ezeike as a specialist in setting up clandestine methamphetamine laboratories with links to one Oscar Ramos-Cardenas, alleged to be a Mexican known for large-scale, industrial-grade methamphetamine production. “From that moment, Ezeike was a marked man. Our officers opened a file on him, and we watched and waited,” the NDLEA chief was quoted as saying in a statement by the agency’s Director, Media and Advocacy, Femi Babafemi. “On 25th August 2026, we received intelligence on the flight itineraries of five Mexican nationals, all identified as methamphetamine experts who were travelling from Mexico to Nigeria. Our analysis left no room for doubt: they were coming to set up an industrial-scale meth laboratory on Nigerian soil. “Working closely with the Nigeria Immigration Service, we ensured that when they landed here in Abuja on 28th August 2026, they were denied entry. They were put on the next available flight back to Mexico. “On that same day, our officers found out that Ezeike had travelled from Enugu to Abuja to receive the visiting Mexicans. His own bank records later confirmed the hotel payment in Abuja that day. The visitors he came to receive were the very men we had just sent back”, Marwa stated. item.title: Nollywood Stars Joke Silva, Funke Akindele, Others Pay Tribute To Pete Edochie
item.description: Nollywood stars Joke Silva, Funke Akindele, Mercy Johnson and others have paid tributes to veteran actor Pete Edochie, who died Wednesday after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer at the age of 79. The actor’s death was announced by his son, Chief Leo Pete Edochie, who confirmed that he died at 12:30 a.m. on November 25, 2026, in Enugu, Nigeria. His death has sparked an outpouring of tributes from colleagues, public leaders and entertainers who have celebrated his remarkable career, influence and legacy. Actress Joke Silva expressed sadness over his death, remembering his playful side. “Uncle Pete…I will miss your teasing. Rest well Sir,” she wrote. Filmmaker and actress Funke Akindele recalled growing up watching Edochie in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart , before eventually sharing the screen with him in the film Egg of Life . She expressed gratitude for his encouragement and the impact he made on younger generations of actors. “Thank you for paving the way for so many of us in Nollywood and for being an inspiration to us over the years. Your work lives on,” she wrote. Similarly, actress Uche Jombo described Edochie as one of Nollywood’s greatest pillars, a master of his craft and a custodian of Nigerian culture. She said the late actor “gave Nigerian storytelling a face, a voice and a legacy that will outlive generations.” “His contribution to Nollywood cannot be measured by the number of films he appeared in, but by the impact he made, the standards he set and the generations of actors he inspired.” Actress Omoni Oboli described his passing as the fall of an iroko tree, writing, “Hmmm 2026! It is well. The Iroko has fallen. Rest in power sir Pete Edochie.” May Edochie, the estranged wife of the late actor’s son, Yul Edochie, also paid tribute, describing him as an institution and a father figure to many. She reflected on the false reports of his death that had circulated over the years, noting that he had continued working despite the rumours. Actor Charles Inojie paid tribute using several of the late actor’s traditional praise names, including Ebube Dike, Ntu Mara Igwe and King of the Forests, before praying for his peaceful rest. While DJ Kaywise thanked him for his contributions to the industry, other entertainers who expressed their grief included comedian Sabinus, who described Edochie as an oracle and a legend. Pete Edochie was born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State. His ancestral roots, however, trace back to Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, in Anambra State. Edochie rose to prominence through his portrayal of Okonkwo in the 1987 Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart . His commanding screen presence, distinctive voice, and memorable delivery of traditional proverbs subsequently made him one of Nollywood’s most recognisable figures. item.title: Ebola Fight Runs Up Against Customs, Rites In Remote DR Congo
item.description: For health workers in the volatile eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), tackling local suspicions is as big a problem as combating the Ebola virus that has plagued it for six months. In the rural community of Bulambo-Isale, AFP saw a small crowd gather this week along a dirt track, determined to prevent an ambulance bringing the body of a local Ebola victim for burial. Victims of the highly contagious haemorrhagic fever, which spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids, must be interred in sealed body bags to prevent infection spreading from the corpse. Burial ceremonies are conducted by specially trained health workers, anonymous in protective hazmat suits, some of whom locals allege are brought in from outside the community and do not speak the local languages. In this file photo taken on March 09, 2019 Health workers are seen inside the ‘red zone’ of an Ebola treatment centre, which was attacked in the early hours of the morning in Butembo. – Democratic Republic of Congo’s government on June 25, 2020 officially declared an end to an epidemic of Ebola that broke out in the east of the troubled country in August 2018 and went on to claim 2,277 lives. (Photo by JOHN WESSELS / AFP) But custom dictates that the deceased be buried by their own family and their body be allowed to fuse with the earth of their ancestors. “The authorities have imposed the Ebola response on locals without first making sure how they interpret it,” grumbled Patricien Kambale, who became a livestock farmer after university. “The sick victim gets carted away in a vehicle and locals don’t know where they’re being taken. Then we learn later that the person has died so locals think the doctors are using poisoned medicine to kill people,” he said. Suspicions of ‘profiteering’ Health workers in Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) simulate with the help of an Outbreak Response Advisor admission protocols of suspected cases during a training by medical charity, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) to reinforce regional emergency response capacity for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo Locals say they are distrustful of Congolese authorities, who have a reputation for corruption and nepotism. Left to cope with the miseries inflicted by myriad armed groups that have stalked their mineral-rich region for more than three decades, they fear their customs and lives matter little to the powers that be. Wilson Kasyani, chief doctor for the Vuhovi health district that includes Bulambo-Isale, a rural settlement in North Kivu province, was worried for the ambulance and its occupants. “Weapons are everywhere” in the mountainous region, he said.
